detailed_rationale:
Cohance Lifesciences (the entity formed from the RA Chem Pharma / Suven Pharmaceuticals combination, now under an Advent International-backed promoter group) is a Hyderabad-based CDMO ranking among the top-5 domestic providers of high-end pharmaceutical/fine-chemical intermediates, spanning process R&D through late-stage clinical and commercial manufacturing for global innovator pharma customers.

The recent quarterly trend is a genuine deterioration, not a base-effect illusion: revenue peaked around Rs.840cr in Q4 FY25 (Mar 2025) and has since stepped down to a Rs.545-619cr range through FY26, while net profit has fallen much faster -- from Rs.117cr in the peak quarter to just Rs.8.3cr in Q4 FY26 -- with operating margin compressing from ~27% to ~16%. This matches the quant data's growth_divergence_flag (trailing 3y revenue CAGR ~19% versus the latest 1y revenue growth of -13%). Alongside the P&L softening, working-capital metrics have deteriorated meaningfully: working-capital days expanded from ~74 to ~175 and debtor days from ~87 to ~110, while borrowings jumped from ~Rs.65cr (Mar 2024) to ~Rs.400cr (Mar 2026). Most notably, screener.in's own shareholding-pattern data flags that promoters have pledged 94.6% of their holding -- an unusually high pledge ratio. This may partly reflect the post-merger, PE-sponsor-backed promoter structure (financing/collateral tied to the RA Chem-Suven combination) rather than pure operating distress, but we could not independently verify the precise reason for the pledge, and either way it materially raises the risk profile of the equity.

Taken together -- a CDMO business with real global-outsourcing tailwinds (China+1 diversification of pharma supply chains), but a company currently showing slowing/declining revenue, sharply compressed margins, rising working-capital stress, rising debt, and a very high promoter pledge -- this is a name where the near-term numbers and the balance-sheet-reality checks both argue for caution well beyond routine noise.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score is Hold (3y and 1y both Hold) and the asymmetric-override rule bars us from converting a Hold to a Sell on our own judgment, however strong our concerns. We keep the recommendation at Hold but escalate, because the combination of a revenue/profit collapse, working-capital deterioration, rising debt, and a 94.6% promoter pledge is squarely the kind of real analytical tension -- not stale data, not routine uncertainty -- that a portfolio manager should weigh directly rather than have silently absorbed into a Hold.
summary: Cohance Lifesciences is a well-regarded pharma CDMO (contract manufacturer) benefiting from global supply-chain diversification away from China, but its most recent quarters show revenue and profit both declining sharply from a year-ago peak, working-capital days stretching out, and debt rising. We also note that promoters have pledged the large majority of their holding, per public shareholding data. We rate the stock a Hold, but flag these as genuine, current-quarter concerns rather than background noise -- this is a name to watch closely rather than treat as a steady compounder right now.
positive_para: Cohance operates in a CDMO segment with real structural tailwinds: global pharmaceutical innovators are actively diversifying manufacturing and intermediate sourcing away from China, and Indian CDMOs with process-chemistry capability are direct beneficiaries. The company's position among the top domestic providers of high-end intermediates and its exposure to global innovator relationships give it a business model that, if execution stabilizes, has genuine multi-year growth runway independent of the Indian domestic pharma cycle.
negative_para: The numbers right now argue for real caution: revenue has fallen from a ~Rs.840cr peak quarter to a ~Rs.545-619cr range, net profit has collapsed far faster than revenue (from ~Rs.117cr to ~Rs.8.3cr in the latest quarter), and operating margin has compressed by roughly 11 percentage points. Working-capital days nearly doubled/2.5x'd and debtor days have lengthened, both consistent with either slower collections, inventory buildup, or softer end-demand -- any of which would matter for cash generation. Debt has grown roughly six-fold off a small base. Most strikingly, screener.in's shareholding data shows promoters have pledged 94.6% of their stake; we could not confirm from public sources whether this reflects deal-financing structure from the RA Chem-Suven combination or genuine promoter liquidity stress, but a pledge this large is a real overhang regardless of cause -- forced-sale risk exists if the pledge is ever invoked.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a trailing PE in the mid-90s (elevated further by the depressed latest-quarter earnings base), the multiple only makes sense if one believes the current revenue/margin dip is a temporary, order-timing-driven CDMO lumpiness rather than a structural slowdown, and that working-capital stress resolves without further debt buildup. Given the magnitude of the recent profit collapse and the promoter-pledge overhang, we would call this rich for the currently demonstrated earnings power -- the multiple is pricing a clean recovery story that the last few quarters have not yet delivered.
escalation_reason: Compounding red flags in the same name: revenue down from a ~Rs.840cr peak quarter to ~Rs.545-619cr, net profit down from ~Rs.117cr to ~Rs.8.3cr in the latest quarter, working-capital days near-doubling, debtor days lengthening, debt up roughly six-fold off a small base, and -- most materially -- screener.in shareholding data showing promoters have pledged 94.6% of their holding. Individually any one of these might be routine; together, in a name the quant model still scores Hold, this looks like a genuine Hold-vs-Sell judgment call the PM should make directly, especially given we could not independently confirm whether the pledge reflects deal-financing structure or promoter distress.
